questions.text: Do you have a job, or are you studying?
questions.say: Good afternoon. My name is Emma, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about what you do. Do you have a job, or are you studying?

questions.text: Do you prefer to work or study in the morning or in the evening?
questions.say: Do you prefer to work or study in the morning or in the evening?

questions.text: Who do you usually ask for help with your work or studies?
questions.say: Who do you usually ask for help with your work or studies?

questions.text: Do you usually work or study alone, or with other people?
questions.say: Do you usually work or study alone, or with other people?

questions.text: Do you often travel by train?
questions.say: Now let's move on to talk about trains. Do you often travel by train?

questions.text: Did you travel by train when you were a child?
questions.say: Did you travel by train when you were a child?

questions.text: Do you like travelling by train? Why or why not?
questions.say: Do you like travelling by train? Why or why not?
Now let's move on to talk about patience. Are you a patient person?

questions.text: What kinds of things make you impatient?
questions.say: What kinds of things make you impatient?

questions.text: Do you think you have become more patient as you have got older?
questions.say: Do you think you have become more patient as you have got older?

cueCard.topic: Describe a creative person whose work you like.
points: what kind of work they do
cueCard.explain: and explain why you like their work.

questions.text: Describe a creative person whose work you like.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a creative person whose work you like. You should say: who this person is; what kind of work they do; how you discovered their work; and explain why you like their work.

questions.text: Have you ever tried to do the same kind of creative work?
questions.say: Thank you. Have you ever tried to do the same kind of creative work?

questions.text: Do you think everyone is creative in some way?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a creative person whose work you like, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all creativity. Do you think everyone is creative in some way?

questions.text: How can schools help children to be more creative?
questions.say: How can schools help children to be more creative?

questions.text: Is creativity important in jobs that are not artistic?
questions.say: Is creativity important in jobs that are not artistic?

questions.text: Should governments spend money on the arts?
questions.say: Now let's talk about the arts. Should governments spend money on the arts?

questions.text: Why do some people never go to galleries or the theatre?
questions.say: Why do some people never go to galleries or the theatre?

questions.text: Will computers ever be able to create art as well as people can?
questions.say: Will computers ever be able to create art as well as people can?
